subject: Revised plan: we launch the new billing page on 3 March. Before that, a two-week beta with 50 existing customers runs from 14 February. If more than 2% of beta payments fail, we push the launch and keep the old page. The old page stays live behind a flag for 30 days after launch so we can switch back in minutes. Support has not been briefed yet.
priors: There is no way back if the new billing page breaks payments after launch.
Nothing is tested with real customers before the launch date.
Support has not been told about the change, so tickets on launch day will go unanswered.

subject: Revised plan: hire one senior backend engineer at $185k instead of two juniors, because the payments rewrite needs someone who has shipped a ledger before. We checked: our current runway is 19 months, and the senior hire takes it to 17. Two of our engineers will interview for ledger experience using a take-home based on our real schema. We have not asked the team whether they want a senior above them.
priors: The plan does not say what the hire does to runway.
Nothing in the interview checks for the ledger experience the plan says it needs.
The plan assumes two juniors would be slower without any evidence.

subject: Revised plan: raise the Team plan from $12 to $15 per seat for new customers only on 1 April. Existing customers keep $12 for 12 months. We will watch trial-to-paid conversion weekly, and if it falls more than 3 points below the 8-week average for two weeks in a row, we roll the price back. Sales will get a one-page note on the change a week before.
priors: Raising the price on existing customers risks churn the plan never prices.
There is no signal or threshold that would make the team undo the change.
The plan does not say whether competitors have moved their prices.

subject: Revised plan: move error tracking from our current vendor to a cheaper one to save $900 a month. We will run both side by side for two weeks and compare alert counts on the same incidents. The cheaper vendor's contract is month to month. We still have not checked whether it supports our on-prem customers' data residency needs.
priors: Switching blind risks missing alerts the current vendor catches.
A long contract would lock us in if the new vendor is worse.
Two on-prem customers need data residency, and nothing says the new vendor supports it.

subject: Revised plan: start a weekly product email to all 4,000 free users on Mondays. Each email has one feature and one customer story. We will stop if unsubscribes pass 1.5% on any send. We send from a new subdomain, warmed up over three weeks first.
priors: There is no stopping rule if people start unsubscribing.
Sending 4,000 emails from the main domain cold could hurt deliverability for transactional mail.
The plan does not say who writes the emails each week.

subject: Revised plan: ask the team to come to the office on Tuesdays and Thursdays from May. We surveyed the team: 9 of 14 said two fixed days would help them. People more than an hour away can choose one day instead. We will review after eight weeks using the same survey.
priors: The plan does not show the team wants office days at all.
A fixed two-day rule ignores people with long commutes.
There is no point at which the policy is reviewed or dropped.
